title: HTTP handlers with bounded requests
summary: Read a JSON body with a size limit and answer with the right status code.

scenario.briefing: The campus status endpoint accepts JSON from a dashboard. A malformed or oversized body must not exhaust memory or produce a misleading success response.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Check the method and URL before you read any data.
Track the byte count inside the data listener.
Answer 413 as soon as the count passes the limit, then stop reading.
Wrap JSON.parse in try/catch and answer 400 from the catch block.

misconceptions.description: Buffering the whole body without a limit.
misconceptions.testDescription: The body is capped at 16 KB and rejected with 413.
misconceptions.feedback: A large body can exhaust memory. Count bytes and reject with 413 once the limit is passed.

misconceptions.description: Calling JSON.parse without a catch block.
misconceptions.testDescription: Malformed JSON is caught and answered with 400.
misconceptions.feedback: Malformed JSON throws. Catch the parse failure and return 400 instead of letting the exception escape.

misconceptions.description: Believing an uncaught exception only affects one request.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Selecting the statement that an uncaught exception only affects that one request.
misconceptions.feedback: An uncaught exception can end the request without a response and may reach the process boundary. Handle the failure in the request path.

sections.title: Requests arrive as streams
sections.body: Node emits the body in chunks. Count bytes as they arrive and stop accepting data once the limit is crossed, before the buffer grows without bound.

sections.title: Status codes are the contract
sections.body: 201 means a resource was created, 400 means the client sent invalid JSON, and 413 means the body is too large. The client should not have to read a message to learn which case occurred.

vocabulary.definition: A piece of the request body emitted by the readable stream.
The maximum number of bytes a handler accepts for a body.
The three-digit result that tells the client how the request was handled.

steps.title: Handle a JSON status update
steps.prompt: Edit server.ts. Accept POST /status, read at most 16 KB of JSON, return 201 with the stored status, 400 for invalid JSON, and 413 when the body is too large.

tests.description: The body is capped at 16 KB and rejected with 413.
Malformed JSON is caught and answered with 400.
A valid update is stored and answered with 201 JSON.

hints: Reject methods and paths that are not POST /status.
Count bytes inside the data listener.
Answer 413 and stop reading once the limit is passed.
Guard JSON.parse with try/catch and answer 400.

steps.title: Request handling

statements.label: A request body should be bounded before it is buffered in memory.
JSON.parse throws on malformed input, so the handler must catch that failure.
A newly created resource is normally answered with 201.
An uncaught exception in a request handler only affects that one request.

steps.explanation: A readable request body can be larger than memory. Counting bytes and rejecting early keeps the service alive, while a guarded parse turns malformed input into a 400 instead of a crash.
hints: Check which statements match the streaming handler.
A body is unlimited until you enforce a limit.
An uncaught exception can end the request without a response.
